Note::NlpAccessor::to_greek¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::to_greek() const

Romanize Greek Letters Into ASCII¶

to_greek() replaces every Greek letter in each cell with a Latin approximation of its sound: Α/α → a, Θ/θ → th, Χ/χ → ch, Ψ/ψ → ps, Ω/ω → o, and so on. Use it to render Greek names, terms, or math-variable names in a Latin-only context.

What is converted¶

  • Both cases fold to lower-case Latin. Α and α both become a; the method does not preserve capitalization.

  • Accented (monotonic) vowels are handled: ά έ ή ί ό ύ ώ and their capitals map to the same base as the unaccented letter (ά → a), as do the dialytika forms ϊ ϋ ΐ ΰ.

  • Combining diacritics are dropped, so to_nfd().nlp().to_greek() also handles polytonic Greek (breathings and the circumflex), which is stored as a base letter plus separate marks.

  • The word-final sigma ς maps to s, the same as σ/Σ.

Any character that is not Greek — Latin letters, digits, spaces, punctuation — passes through unchanged, so mixed-script text keeps its non-Greek parts intact.

The operation is shape-preserving and cell-independent, works on UTF-8 text (a bytes-mode Note is rejected with Note::NlpAccessor::to_greek requires a UTF-8 text Note (not bytes)), and returns a fresh UTF-8 Note.

Example 1: Accented Words¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Ελλάς", "θεωρία", "Χάος", "ΩΜΕΓΑ"}).nlp().to_greek())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["ellas", "theoria", "chaos", "omega"]

The tonos on ά is folded away; ΩΜΕΓΑ (all caps) still comes out lower-case.

Example 2: Mixed Script Keeps Its Latin Parts¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"alpha=Α beta=β"}).nlp().to_greek() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["alpha=a beta=b"]

Only Α and β change; alpha=, , =, and beta are untouched.

Example 3: Final Sigma¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"λόγος"}).nlp().to_greek() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["logos"]

Example 4: Polytonic Greek Via NFD¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"ἄνθρωπος"}).to_nfd().nlp().to_greek() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["anthropos"]

ἄ carries a breathing mark and an acute accent. to_nfd splits it into α plus two combining marks; to_greek maps the α and drops the marks.

See Also¶

  • Note::NlpAccessor::to_cyrillic: the same idea for the Cyrillic alphabet.

  • Note::NlpAccessor::to_ascii: fold Latin accents and replace anything else with ?.

  • Note::to_nfd: decompose accents so polytonic Greek transliterates cleanly.
